title: Basis of the Annual Rent Charged on a Lease of Safe Deposit Boxes
content:
Rent on Safe Deposit Boxes is charged once per rental year of 12 months, in advance, on the rent due date, and the lease renews automatically at the end of each term.

## The two quantities

**The gross rent** is the annual rent for the size leased, taken before branch adjustment and before any discount, increased or reduced by the branch adjustment percent carried by the rental's branch, and the result rounded half-up to the cent.

**The net rent charged** is the gross rent less the one discount allocated to that rental for that rental year, and the result rounded half-up to the cent.

The branch adjustment acts on the annual rent for the size. The discount acts on the gross rent that results, not on the annual rent before adjustment, and each of the two amounts is rounded half-up to the cent as it is arrived at.

## Notices

A rent notice is sent 30 days before each rent due date. A change in the rent takes effect only at a renewal falling at least 30 days after notice of the change.

## A year's rent worked through on hypothetical facts

Take a 3x10 Safe Deposit Box held at Charlotte SouthPark, and suppose that the discount allocated to that rental for the year is 13 percent.

1. The annual rent for that size before branch adjustment and before discount is $85.00.
2. Charlotte SouthPark carries 15 percent added to the base rent, so the gross rent is $85.00 increased by 15 percent, which is $97.75. Rounded half-up to the cent it remains $97.75.
3. The net rent charged is $97.75 less 13 percent, which is $85.0425, rounded half-up to the cent to give $85.04.

The figure charged for the year is therefore $85.04. The discount of 13 percent in this illustration is a hypothetical input chosen to work the calculation through; it is not a rate the bank offers.

Had the same box been held at Greensboro Main Office, whose vault carries no adjustment, the gross rent would have been $85.00 and the same discount would have given $73.95.
